title: He made the sea carry your ships.
subtitle: Trade and travel as a gift to thank for
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}ordered the sea to carry ships{/idea}, so people could seek His bounty {reward}in commercial and business transactions{/reward}, and be thankful for provisions brought from distant lands.
now: The bananas in your kitchen crossed an ocean. Your phone was shipped in a container. {reward}Half of what you own floated to you.{/reward} The verse asks you to notice and thank.
old: Imported goods are just what shops sell.
new: The sea carrying my things to me is a favour from Allah.
try: Pick one item in your home that came from overseas and thank Allah for it.

title: All in the heavens and earth, put at your service.
subtitle: Everything is from Him alone
then: Ibn Kathir names {reward}the stars, the mountains, the seas, the rivers{/reward} and all that people use. Ibn Abbas said: {idea}everything is from Allah{/idea}, without rivals. It is a sign for people who think deeply.
now: You flick a switch and the lights come on. You open a tap. A GPS satellite finds you in seconds. {idea}All of it rests on a world that was made to serve you.{/idea}
old: The world just happens to be useful to us.
new: The world was put at my service, all of it from Him.
try: Spend one minute tonight thinking about one thing in nature that serves you every day.

title: Tell the believers to forgive those who harm them.
subtitle: Leaving the recompense to Allah
then: Ibn Kathir says in the beginning of Islam, believers were told to {idea}forgive and endure the harm{/idea} of the idolaters, so that their hearts might incline to Islam. Mujahid said those who hope not for Allah's Days are those who {trap}do not appreciate His favours{/trap}. Allah Himself will repay each.
now: A relative said something cruel at a family dinner. You replay it at night and plan your comeback. {idea}You can let it go and leave the account with Allah.{/idea}
old: If I forgive, they get away with it.
new: Forgiving does not erase their deed. It hands the account to Allah.
try: Think of one person who hurt you and say: Allah, I leave this with You.

title: Your good is for you, your harm is on you.
subtitle: Every deed comes back to its doer
then: Right after telling believers to forgive, the verse reminds them: {reward}good is for yourself{/reward}, {trap}evil is against yourself{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says all will return to Allah on the Day, when people and their actions are shown, and He will repay good with good and evil with evil.
now: You hold the door, stay late to help a colleague, and no one says thanks. It stings. {reward}That deed is filed under your name, not theirs.{/reward}
old: When my kindness goes unnoticed, it was wasted.
new: Every good I do is for me, noticed or not.
try: Do one kind thing today that no one will ever know was you.

title: Scripture, wisdom and prophethood were given before.
subtitle: The Children of Israel received great gifts
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah mentions the favours He gave the Children of Israel: {reward}revealing Divine Books, sending Messengers, and granting kingship{/reward}, good food and drink, and preference over the nations of their time.
now: You grew up with the Quran in the house, a masjid down the road, parents who prayed. {idea}Those are gifts many never had.{/idea} The question is what you are doing with them.
old: Having been raised with faith means I am on safe ground.
new: Being given much means I will be asked about much.
try: List three religious blessings you were given without asking, and thank Allah for each.

title: They split after knowledge came, out of rivalry.
subtitle: Division born of envy, not ignorance
then: Ibn Kathir says they were given clear proofs, {trap}yet they differed among themselves after the proof came, out of transgression against each other{/trap}. He says the verse is {idea}a warning to the Muslim Ummah as well{/idea}, not to take the same path.
now: Two masjid committees in the same town stop speaking. Both know the same verses. {trap}It is not knowledge they lack. It is the ego in the room.{/trap}
old: Arguments in a community are about who is right.
new: Many splits come from rivalry, after everyone already knew the truth.
try: Next time you disagree with a fellow Muslim, ask: is this about truth or about winning?

title: You are set on a clear way, so follow it.
subtitle: Not the desires of those who do not know
then: Ibn Kathir says this tells the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}follow what was revealed to you from your Lord{/idea}, and do not follow the desires of those who do not know. It comes right after the warning about splitting.
now: Everyone on your timeline has an opinion on how to live, what to want, what to drop. {trap}Their loudness is not knowledge.{/trap} You already have a way. Walk it.
old: I should shape my life around what most people think is right.
new: I have been given a clear way. Others' desires are not a guide.
try: Mute one account today that keeps pulling you away from your values.

title: Allah is the protector of the mindful.
subtitle: Wrongdoers back each other, and it fails
then: Ibn Kathir asks what the loyalty of wrongdoers to each other will give them: {trap}only more loss and ruin{/trap}. But {reward}Allah is the Protector of those who have taqwa{/reward}, and He brings them out of darkness into light.
now: The group at work that covers for each other's shortcuts. It feels safe to be inside it. {reward}Allah's protection does not depend on being in any crowd.{/reward}
old: I am safest when I am inside the strong group.
new: The One who protects the mindful is the only backing that holds.
try: Do the right thing in one small situation today even if the group does otherwise.

title: Insight for people, and mercy for the certain.
subtitle: The Quran as a way of seeing
then: Ibn Kathir says this refers to the Quran: {idea}a clear insight and evidence for mankind{/idea}, and {reward}a guidance and a mercy for people of certainty{/reward}. Basa'ir means things that help you see.
now: New glasses: suddenly the street signs are sharp and you realise how blurry life was. {idea}The Quran is meant to work like that.{/idea} Not just read, but looked through.
old: The Quran is something I read, then return to my day.
new: The Quran is a lens to see my day through.
try: Carry one verse in mind today and look at one situation through it.

title: Do the wrongdoers think they will be treated alike?
subtitle: Good and evil are never equal
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}the believers and the disbelievers are never equal{/idea}, in this life or the next. Thinking otherwise is a bad thought about Allah's justice. He reports that Tamim ad-Dari once {reward}stood in night prayer until morning reciting only this verse{/reward}.
now: You watch someone cheat their way up at work and do fine. You wonder if being honest was pointless. {idea}The verse says it was never the same, and it will not end the same.{/idea}
old: In the end, the honest and the cheaters end up in the same place.
new: Allah's justice will never treat the doer of good like the doer of evil.
try: Recite this verse slowly once tonight, the way Tamim ad-Dari did, and let it sink in.

title: Created in truth, so each soul gets its due.
subtitle: Justice is built into creation
then: Ibn Kathir explains created with truth as {idea}created in justice{/idea}, so that each person is recompensed for what he earned, and {reward}they will not be wronged{/reward}. It answers the false assumption of the verse before.
now: You were passed over for a promotion you earned. The unfairness sits in your chest. {reward}Nothing you did is lost from the record.{/reward} Full justice is coming.
old: Some of my efforts will just disappear unseen.
new: Creation was built on justice. Every soul gets exactly its due.
try: Think of one unfairness you carry and say: Allah, You are the Just, I trust You with it.

title: Have you seen one who made his desire his god?
subtitle: When wanting becomes the one who commands
then: Ibn Kathir describes one who {trap}abides by his lust: whatever it portrays as good he does, whatever it portrays as evil he leaves{/trap}. Allah left him astray after knowledge reached him, so he no longer hears, understands or sees what would help him.
now: You skip the prayer because you are not in the mood. You buy it because you want it. You say it because it feels good to say. {trap}Who is actually giving the orders?{/trap}
old: Following my feelings is just being true to myself.
new: If my desire always decides, it has become my god.
try: Today, do one good thing you do not feel like doing, just because Allah wants it.
